body:
## Summary

On PP disaggregated prefill, a burst of client cancellations can make the per-stage bootstrap queues diverge: stages stop agreeing on which requests were admitted/aborted, subsequently select different microbatches, and the fixed PP P2P send/recv schedule deadlocks — each rank blocks in a *different* send/recv slot until the NCCL watchdog kills the server a full hour later. Requests keep returning 200 on `/health` the whole time.

Environment where we hit it in production: PP=8 disaggregated prefill (TP=1) + Mooncake KV transfer, HiCache L2-only, 32K-token inputs with ~90% shared prefix, high-concurrency cancellations.

This issue tracks the RCA and the fix series:

- [ ] #34568 — fold HiCache prefetch readiness into the bootstrap consensus (prerequisite; closes the L3-storage readiness divergence gate)
- [ ] #34569 — ordered immutable bootstrap decisions with exactly-once apply (main fix; closes the abort / local KV-failure / metadata-finalize gates)
- [ ] #34570 — PD router: never auto-replay a request that may already be dispatched (stops the router from generating non-idempotent replays that amplify these races)

## Incident signature (how to recognize it)

Align each rank's `Prefill batch` lines by order of appearance (**not** by timestamp — adjacent logical batches legally land in the same second across skewed stages). The signature is: a common prefix, then one wave that only reaches part of the pipeline, with queue counters diverging at the same boundary.

<details>
<summary>Per-rank last batches — the next wave (3072) exists only on PP0–PP3</summary>

```text
[2026-08-11 10:26:57 PP0] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 2, #new-token: 6144, #cached-token: 57728, ... #queue-req: 0, #bootstrap-req: 54, #inflight-req: 6, ...
[2026-08-11 10:26:58 PP0] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 3072, #cached-token: 28864, ... #queue-req: 4, #bootstrap-req: 38, #inflight-req: 6, ...   <-- last wave, PP0–PP3 only

[2026-08-11 10:26:57 PP4] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 2, #new-token: 6144, #cached-token: 57728, ... #queue-req: 0, #bootstrap-req: 52, #inflight-req: 6, ...   <-- PP4 final line
[2026-08-11 10:26:58 PP7] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 2, #new-token: 6144, #cached-token: 57728, ... #queue-req: 0, #bootstrap-req: 40, #inflight-req: 6, ...   <-- PP7 final line
```

Waiting queues at the same moment: `4/3/3/3` on PP0–PP3 vs `0/0/0/0` on PP4–PP7. Note PP7's final 6144 line carries the same `10:26:58` timestamp as PP0's 3072 line — timestamp-based alignment would misread this entirely.

</details>

<details>
<summary>py-spy: all 8 schedulers blocked in different P2P slots (different logical rounds)</summary>

```text
PP0  recv_tensor_dict            <- waiting for output tensor
PP1  _pp_recv_pyobj_from_prev_stage (event_loop @311)   <- waiting for bootstrap consensus msg
PP2  request_receiver._pull_raw_reqs                    <- waiting for request forwarding
PP3  _pp_commit_comm_work (event_loop @246)             <- committing a request send
PP4  _pp_commit_comm_work (event_loop @319)             <- committing a release send
PP5  _pp_commit_comm_work (event_loop @316)             <- committing a consensus send
PP6  _pp_commit_comm_work (event_loop @279)             <- committing a proxy-tensor send
PP7  _pp_recv_pyobj_from_prev_stage (event_loop @311)   <- waiting for bootstrap consensus msg
```

PP3–PP6 sit on the same wait primitive but at four *different* event-loop call sites — the stages are executing different steps of the protocol, not sharing one slow collective. (Line numbers are from the incident build.)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Trigger window: AbortReq-driven failure burst 1–2 s before the divergence, and the sets differ per stage</summary>

```text
[2026-08-11 10:26:57 PP0] Prefill bootstrap failed ... req.rid='48631b68...' ... KVTransferError(...): Aborted by AbortReq.
[2026-08-11 10:26:57 PP0] Prefill bootstrap failed ... req.rid='962899b6...' ... KVTransferError(...): Aborted by AbortReq.
[2026-08-11 10:26:57 PP1] Prefill bootstrap failed ... req.rid='781581fa...' ... KVTransferError(...): Aborted by AbortReq.
[2026-08-11 10:26:58 PP0] Prefill transfer failed  ... req.rid='f815dd84...' ... KVTransferError(...): Aborted by AbortReq.
```

13 bootstrap failures + 1 transfer failure in the window; PP0 and PP1 observed **different** failure sets.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Watchdog fires 3600 s later, on unmatched SEND work (different SeqNum per rank)</summary>

```text
[rank6]:[E811 11:26:58 ...] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=28778, OpType=SEND, ...) ran for 3600029 milliseconds before timing out.
[rank2]:[E811 11:26:58 ...] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=28787, OpType=SEND, ...) ran for 3600098 milliseconds before timing out.
```

Different `SeqNum` on different ranks — the P2P works no longer pair up. The watchdog is a delayed detector here, not the cause; router health-check failures and decode `KVTransferError` are downstream symptoms.

</details>

## Root cause

The PP bootstrap protocol must guarantee that every stage applies the same queue transitions in the same order. The old protocol had four places where a **local** event could rewrite one stage's queue history outside the cross-stage consensus:

1. An uncovered local `KVPoll.Failed` in `pop_bootstrapped()` deleted the request on one stage only.
2. The second ring pass forwarded each stage's local post-apply result rather than a frozen decision.
3. `AbortReq` and bootstrap results had no common order (`Decision N → Abort` on one stage, `Abort → Decision N` on another — both mutate queues).
4. After a PP-wide good decision, metadata finalize could still fail locally and silently `continue` on one stage.

HiCache L3 prefetch readiness was a fifth gate of the same shape, fixed separately in #34568 (our incident was L2-only, which is why that fix alone did not cover it).

## Fix

Enforced invariant (see #34569 for details): **bootstrap queue history may only change through a cross-PP committed decision — PP0 freezes an immutable `(sequence, good, bad)` decision, every stage applies it exactly once and forwards it verbatim; local abort/failure/readiness signals only feed the next decision.** Protocol violations (sequence gap, payload divergence, finalize failure after a good commit) now raise immediately instead of deadlocking for an hour.

Validated with incident-shaped traffic plus deliberate abort storms (80/80 consistent decisions, per-stage failure *proposals* differing while committed sets stayed identical, 0 shape mismatch / gap / watchdog; ~7 h soak, 127543/127569 succeeded, 0 failed).
title: [Bug][PP] PP disaggregated prefill hangs: bootstrap queue history diverges across stages under abort storms (RCA + fix series)
